subject: Ephemeral demo sessions: routing, no-learn commitment, and prompt/response ownership
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-20T09:05:00-08:00
Subject: Ephemeral demo sessions: routing, no-learn commitment, and prompt/response ownership

Team —

Quick summary of a call with Clinica Health this morning. They want a short attachment-free pilot where their EU users will run live demos with real patient-like records (pseudonymized) and they need three things spelled out in our DPA/addendum before legal will sign:

1) A clear "no adaptive training" / no-learning commitment for any data captured during ephemeral demo sessions (they expect an auditable policy).
2) Explicit ownership/entitlement language for prompts and responses generated during those sessions — they want an assertion that their prompts and resulting outputs aren’t re-used to improve models or surfaceable artifacts for other customers.
3) Routing and processing guarantees: EU traffic must be processed onshore (EU region) and any temporary KV/prefix cache must be ephemeral and purged on session end with retention proofs.

They asked for an operational checklist we can hand to their security team (simple, not legalese) plus a DPA addendum draft that calls out the above and points to the operational controls.

Can you sketch a short checklist + technical notes and I’ll put that into a one-page addendum? Also flag anything that would need an SLA or Dedicated capacity commitment (they hinted at a higher throughput pilot).

Thanks —
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Head of Product, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachment: safeguards-checklist-v1.pdf (stated contents: ephemeral session steps, purge verification checklist)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-20T11:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Ephemeral demo sessions: routing, no-learn commitment, and prompt/response ownership

Jonas —

I drafted a short operational checklist (high level) and annotated bits that will need legal language. Key items: 

- Session isolation: each demo session runs in a dedicated ephemeral inference container with KV cache scoped to session id.
- Cache purge: automatic purge on session termination + retention log entry with timestamp and operator id.
- No-learning flag: service-level flag to opt session requests out of telemetry/model-updates (recorded in request headers and logged).
- Output custody: generated outputs stored only for the session timeframe (30 minutes by default) unless customer explicitly requests export.
- Processing location: forced EU region deployment (eur1). We need an onshore routing policy entry and region-affinity enforcement.
- Evidence: audit log export (signed) and a snapshot of the ephemeral container lifecycle for the session.

Notes / asks for infra (Karthik): is the 30-minute default reasonable? We should allow customer-configurable TTL and provide a signed SR for purge. Also, for high throughput demos we may want Dedicated capacity or burst to avoid cross-tenant noisy neighbor risk.

I attached the checklist PDF. Happy to convert to one pager for them.

—Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Senior Director, Enterprise Security (Redwood)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-20T13:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Ephemeral demo sessions: routing, no-learn commitment, and prompt/response ownership

Thanks — quick technical clarifications from infra/runtime: 

- No-learning flag: we already support request-level metadata that prevents telemetry from flowing into model improvement pipelines. We'll need the DPA to require that customers set this header for demo traffic and we will log an immutable entry showing the flag was present.
- KV eviction/purge: we can guarantee deletion from KV and disk within < 5s of session end for ephemeral containers, but full confirmation (signed) requires a background job that creates a signed purge receipt (we can automate).
- TTL: 30 minutes default ok; add ability to set to 0 minutes for strict pilots. If they want longer retention we should handle via export request flow (explicit opt-in).
- Onshore enforcement: routing policy will pin traffic to EUR compute; however, if customer expects specific country residency (e.g., DE only) that's a different ask and will require Dedicated or VPC/private deployment.

Operational implication: to give them signed purge receipts and region pins we need to grant them a short on-boarding window with a staging test and runbook verification. For throughput spikes — recommend reserving Dedicated burst for the pilot (we can propose a 1-month burst credit if sales wants to include as a closing incentive).

Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer, Serving Runtime

From: Elena Rossi <elena@clinica.io>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-23T09:40:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Ephemeral demo sessions: routing, no-learn commitment, and prompt/response ownership

Jonas —

Thanks for the quick recap. A few clarifications from our side after reviewing the checklist: 

1) We need the DPA addendum to include an explicit "no-derive / no-model-improvement" clause that covers: prompts, raw transcripts, attachments provided during sessions, and generated outputs.
2) We also need a way to obtain the signed purge receipt for every session (machine-readable) and an agreed SLA for response time if we ask for proof of deletion.
3) Proof of EU processing must include an address/region statement and the ability for an auditor to validate the container lifecycle (we can share an auditor contact if needed).

On the export: for the pilot we will likely request a handful of session transcripts to seed internal notes. If we explicitly request an export, we will sign a separate export consent form.

Can you share a short addendum and the checklist in Word so our legal/security folks can redline?

Best —
Elena Rossi
Head of Product Security, Clinica Health

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena@clinica.io>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, procurement@clinica.io
Date: 2026-11-27T16:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Ephemeral demo sessions: routing, no-learn commitment, and prompt/response ownership

Elena / team —

Appreciate the specifics — nothing here appears to be a blocker. Next steps I propose: 

1) Kimberly & I will produce a one‑page operational checklist in Word and a short DPA addendum draft that contains: the no-derive clause, a machine-readable purge-receipt definition, and an auditor access clause limited to session lifecycle evidence.
2) Karthik will prepare a short technical appendix describing headers to set (no-learn header name + values), TTL options, and the purge-receipt structure (JSON schema).
3) We will include a proposed pilot SOW item: 1 week staging + 2 weeks pilot, with an optional Dedicated burst (30k tokens/day) and a one-time pilot credit to cover burst costs.
4) I'll attach the initial DPA addendum (redwood-dpa-draft.docx) and the Word checklist to this thread — please expect those in the morning.

If Clinica wants an auditor handshake earlier, share the contact and I'll route to our compliance team.

On the ask for export consent: we will require an explicit signed export consent form before any transcript leaves EU-hosted storage — we will put a template in the addendum.

I'll follow up with attachments and an internal routing SOW.

Thanks —
Jonas
Head of Product, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
